Thanks for the ping, Hannah — I pulled the serving runtime logs and the controller metrics for the 02:00–02:40 UTC window. Quick summary:
- We observed elevated queue build-up on one of the shared batches on 02:05–02:20 UTC because of a third-party networking flap from ProviderX that caused intermittent packet loss for a subset of requests routed through us-east-1a.
- The routing system triggered a degraded-mode fallback for affected shards at 02:06 and recovered fully by 02:23 UTC.
- During the period we classify as "partial degradation" (02:06–02:23) the error rate for the affected route rose ~18–22% and median latency increased from 220ms to ~940ms.

How our SLA calculation applies:
- The SLA defines availability at the per-route level measured in successful request rate per-minute across the customer's pinned model variant.
- Scheduled maintenance windows must be pre-announced in the console or via the customer incident channel; we have no pre-announce for that window.
- Appendix A (partial degradation credits) indicates fractional credits when availability is reduced but not fully down; the formula uses weighted minutes of reduced availability.

I attached the raw service logs (service-metrics-0514.log) and a brief calc worksheet. Based on our standard formula, the event translates to a 10% prorated credit on the monthly hosting component for the affected route.

Recommendation: Offer BrightWave the 10% credit for May's hosting line and document the root cause as "third-party network provider outage; partial degradation". We should include the log excerpt and our minutes-weighted calc when we respond.

-Marissa

Thanks again for the detailed report and the CSV you shared. We investigated on our side and validated the partial degradation you observed. Summary and proposal:

What happened:
- On 2026-05-14 between 02:06–02:23 UTC a third-party networking issue in ProviderX caused intermittent packet loss for a subset of our serving shard routing. This produced a measurable increase in error rates and latency for your keyword-extraction route (see attached log excerpt).

How we calculated the credit:
- Per Appendix A of the SLA (see attached contract excerpt), we compute a minute-weighted reduction in successful requests for the affected route and translate that into a prorated credit on the hosting component.
- Using our standard worksheet the event maps to a 10% credit against May's hosting charges for the route in question. Attached is the small calc document (credit-proposal-draft.pdf) and the supporting logs.

Proposed next steps:
1) If you accept, we will apply the 10% credit to your May invoice and send an updated billing statement.
2) We'll include the incident summary in the monthly reliability report and add a post-mortem note about ProviderX's network flap.
3) If you would like a longer-term mitigation plan (e.g., multi-region routing or dedicated shard capacity), I'm happy to set up a quick architect session.

If you'd like anything adjusted before we finalize the credit, tell me what you want and we'll take it to commercial leadership.
